title: No charges in police shooting of Black man in N.D.G., Crown declares
article: Crown prosecutors will not be pressing criminal charges against two Montreal police officers in the shooting death of Sheffield Matthews, a Black man who was killed in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce in October 2020.

The Directeur des poursuites criminelles et pénales announced the decision Wednesday, saying there wasn't enough evidence to warrant prosecution, after studying the report produced by the Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes (BEI), which investigates cases involving police forces.

At 5:50 a.m. on the morning of Oct 29, 2020, officers responded to a 911 call about a man who appeared to be in crisis and screaming, near Côte-St-Luc Rd. and West Hill Ave. Police said the man came toward them with a knife, then moved toward a city bus. He ignored calls to drop the knife, and advanced on one police officer, who tried to run away. With the man still in pursuit, the officer turned and fired twice. His partner, on the other side of the street, also fired a shot. Ballistics reports found three shots were fired, but only one was fatal, fired at a distance of less than one metre by the officer who was being pursued.
The crown found that based on the report, the police officer used necessary force to protect himself, after trying repeatedly to speak with the man and ask him to drop his knife.

A vigil was held for Matthews, 41, a week after his shooting. Organizers declared it was another example of how police are not properly trained to handle individuals in the throes of a mental health crisis.
